image_description: A grey whale breaching the surface of blue water, showing its head and upper back. The skin is dark with mottled white patches (barnacles). A watermark text '© Roi Hlaker' is visible across the center.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears somewhat consistent with a whale, but the specific anatomical detail of 'two blowholes' is not clearly visible or distinguishable due to image resolution and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly shows the characteristic mottled pattern with white barnacle patches typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the back shows a series of small humps (knuckles) rather than a single large dorsal fin, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior part of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the texture and coloration match the description.
